Subject: Question on live-output metering for partial responses and reconnects

Hi Camila,

Quick question as we're finalizing our cost model for the pilot: when a user session is streaming a long generated note and the client disconnects (network flake) before the model finishes, how will Redwood bill that? Specifically:

- Do you bill only for tokens successfully sent to the client, or for tokens the model produced server-side even if the socket dropped?
- If the client retries the same request (without an idempotency key), are those re-generated tokens billed again?
- If we implement reconnect/resume semantics, is there a recommended pattern to avoid double-billing?

We saw a spike last week where 15% of sessions disconnected mid-stream and we want to make sure we model costs correctly. Any documentation or rate-card notes you can send would be great.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Mercer

Acme Health

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear examples, and sorry you hit the spike. Short answers up front, then I'll attach the rate card and loop in engineering for details: 

- Billing: Redwood bills for tokens that were generated by the model (server-side) — i.e., tokens that consumed compute — not strictly for bytes successfully ACKed by the TCP socket. That means if a model generates N tokens and the connection drops before you receive some of those, those tokens are counted. 

- Retries: If a retry issues a new request that causes the model to re-generate the same output, that will be billed again unless you use idempotency or session-resume semantics.

- Recommended pattern: use an idempotency token or the streaming session_id header (we surface X-Redwood-Session and X-Redwood-Resume-Token) so the runtime can deduplicate replays, and implement a short-lived checkpointing approach (send finalization event) so the service knows the session completed. We have an example implementation I'll attach.

I've attached the hosted API rate card (Q1 2026) and a one-page note on best practices. If you'd like, we can offer a small courtesy credit for the spike while we work through optimizing client-side resume behavior — I'll confirm with finance/CS.

Camila — thanks for looping us in. Technical notes:

- Current billing is tied to completed model token generation. The serving runtime increments usage counters at generation commitment time (when token is materialized), independent of socket state.
- Explicit client cancel (user hits cancel) emits a finalization event to the runtime if client calls the cancel endpoint; those tokens are still counted because compute was used, but we record a cancellation flag for downstream analytics and possible ops credits.
- For retries: we can support idempotency via an idempotency-key header (recommended) — if provided within a 5 minute window we dedupe and avoid recharging. We also expose an X-Redwood-Resume-Token for stream checkpoints.
- For Acme pilot: we can enable a transient dedupe mode scoped to their tenant for 30 days (engineers can flip a tenant flag) which will attempt to deduplicate retried requests at the host level. This is not on by default because of memory/kv cost at scale.

Operationally, if we enable tenant-scoped dedupe for Acme we should:
1) Flag the tenant in the routing layer
2) Enable 5-minute idempotency window for streaming sessions
3) Monitor for duplicated generation events and report weekly

I think this mitigates most of their concerns. On the credit ask: recommending a one-time invoice credit equal to the estimated extra tokens from the spike (we can approximate using their logs) but capped at $7k for the pilot.

- Priyom

Hi Alex & Sanjay — quick update after internal review: 

1) Billing semantics: tokens generated by the model are the primary billing unit (server-side generation). Explicit client cancel and network disconnects are treated the same for token accounting, but we tag cancellations in our usage reports for visibility.

2) Retries & dedupe: please use an idempotency-key for requests; we recommend sending X-Redwood-Session and X-Redwood-Resume-Token for long-running streams. For the pilot, we will enable a tenant-scoped dedupe window (5 minutes) to reduce accidental double-billing from retries. Engineers have route-level toggles to enable this for your tenant.

3) Credit: we've approved a one-time credit up to $5,000 to offset the March pilot spike while you adopt resume tokens. This is separate from pricing/discount discussions. If you move to a committed reserved tier, we can discuss deeper discounts.
